tx-71-001.title: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code § 71.001
tx-71-001.note: Defines fur-bearing animal with a closed list of species that does not include squirrels or flying squirrels.

fl-class3.title: Florida Administrative Code Chapter 68A-6, Captive Wildlife
fl-class3.note: FWC's captive wildlife chapter sets the Class I, II and III tiers, with Class III requiring only a free personal-pet permit.

nc-113-272-5.title: North Carolina General Statutes § 113-272.5
nc-113-272-5.note: North Carolina's captivity-license statute, which bars issuing a license for a wild animal acquired merely as a pet.

ny-11-0512.title: New York Environmental Conservation Law § 11-0512
ny-11-0512.note: Bars knowingly possessing, harboring, selling or importing any wild animal for use as a pet, with the special license path set out in ECL § 11-0515(1) and 6 NYCRR Part 175.

wi-nr-10-02.title: Wisconsin Administrative Code NR 10.02
wi-nr-10-02.note: Lists Wisconsin's protected wild animals, which may not be taken, transported or possessed without DNR authorization.

il-520-5.title: Illinois Wildlife Code, 520 ILCS 5
il-520-5.note: Places ownership of wild birds and mammals in the state and requires an IDNR permit to hold protected native wildlife, including tree squirrels, in captivity.

oh-1531.title: Ohio Revised Code Chapter 1531
oh-1531.note: Ohio's Division of Wildlife chapter, which defines game quadrupeds (including the flying squirrel) and requires a permit to possess native wildlife.

md-10-901.title: Maryland Natural Resources Code § 10-901
md-10-901.note: Opens Maryland's Captive Wildlife subtitle with legislative findings supporting strict regulation of possessing wildlife native to the state.

hi-4-71-6-prohibited.title: Hawaii Administrative Rules § 4-71-6, List of Prohibited Animals
hi-4-71-6-prohibited.note: HDOA's prohibited species list, which bans the entire squirrel family Sciuridae except two zoo-exhibition species and university-research marmots.

ny-dangerous-animal.title: 6 NYCRR § 180.1, Animals Dangerous to Health or Welfare
ny-dangerous-animal.note: The regulation behind DEC's Dangerous Animal License, listing canids, bears, felids, primates and venomous reptiles among others, with no parrot or cockatoo family included.

wi-datcp-birds.title: Wisconsin Statutes § 169.01(25m)
wi-datcp-birds.note: Defines pet bird as a non-native, non-endangered, non-migratory psittacine or soft-bill bird, the category Wisconsin's captive wildlife law leaves unregulated.

ut-r657-3b.title: Utah Administrative Code R657-3b
ut-r657-3b.note: Governs certificates of registration for bird and mammal species; its Table 3b-1 classifies non-native Family Psittacidae as noncontrolled, needing no certificate.
